correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge3\), \(\ell\ge1\) and positive repeated arm weights, the cycle Fourier transform gives Jacobi blocks H(mu). Strict interlacing against the fixed trailing principal minor gives disjoint branch spectral intervals; endpoint nonvanishing and positive Hellmann--Feynman derivative exclude other eigenvalue collisions. For each degenerate k,n-k pair, the leaf observation matrix has rank 1 exactly at n|2k(s-s0) for every input site. A cyclic annihilator argument counts floor((g-1)/2) such pairs per branch. Spectral interpolation converts these exact PBH ranks into the claimed full Kalman rank. The extracted checker gives 1126 finite cross-checks, including 40 exact rational Kalman ranks; these are supplemental, not the infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The cycle theorem alone does not imply that rank defects multiply by \(\ell+1\) in the rooted product, because different fiber branches could in principle collide or a terminal-coordinate could vanish. Both possibilities are excluded by a nonstandard uniform Jacobi interlacing and endpoint argument proved here. A general published rooted-product controllability theorem, if found, could nevertheless imply this claim; this remains a residual risk.

originality.rationale: The full all-positive-weight rank-lifting law for identically rooted path decorations is not stated or implied by the inspected pure-cycle PBH literature, periodic infinite transition-operator spectrum, or published finite-cycle frame optimization. Literature risk persists concerning the inaccessible complete 2017 generated-graph source; available abstract neither proves stronger coverage nor supports certifying its absence.

value.rationale: For a natural family of cycle-based sensor/actuator networks, the theorem yields complete ranks for any subset, sharp minimum input count and all successful two-input placements, uniformly across every positive repeated arm-weight profile and any pendant length. The nontrivial structural band-separation lemma explains why adding arbitrarily many interior vertices changes the rank deficit by an exact factor yet leaves the arithmetic actuator criterion intact. This directly informs controllable terminal placements and weight robustness, beyond an isolated example or computation.
